subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt the open fork PR, replace it with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or close that branch before queueing another fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the issue has an open conflicting fork PR with closing syntax, so automation should not create a competing fix PR until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale fork path and land a current-main fix covering sanitizer use plus sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add the missing regression/proof coverage, and review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave the issue blocked on the existing conflicting fork PR despite its stale head and lack of current-main coverage.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale fork path and land a current-main fix covering sanitizer use plus sync and async displayName hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent routing signal on the affected Gateway session-list organization and TUI surfaces.
